mainEntity.name: When should I stop trying to build my website with AI and hire a professional?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A simple DIY build is reasonable when the site has few pages, low-risk forms, straightforward content, and no unusual integrations. Professional help becomes more valuable when the project involves custom software, complex data flows, ecommerce, accessibility remediation, migration, or a costly failure.

Context: AI reduces some drafting and coding effort, but it does not remove requirements analysis, testing, deployment, maintenance, or troubleshooting. Community reports also highlight difficulty with debugging and exporting projects.

Key factors:
- Business impact of downtime or errors
- Technical complexity and integrations
- Owner’s available time
- Need for ongoing support or handoff

Practical guidance: Ask for a written scope, ownership map, test plan, backup process, and handoff documentation before hiring help. For DIY work, begin with a contained page or workflow rather than the entire business system.

Run My AI Business’s educational material can help an owner understand the work before deciding who should perform it.
acceptedAnswer.description: DIY works for simple, low-risk sites. Consider professional help for custom software, complex integrations, sensitive data, accessibility problems, migration, ecommerce, or situations where downtime and errors would be expensive.
